The number of students studying in class X from school P forms approximately what percentage of the total number of students studying in class X from all schools together?.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of students in class X from school P = 144

Total number of students in class X from all schools = 910

**Concept and Formula used:**

Percentage = (Part / Whole) × 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ Percentage = (144 / 910) × 100

⇒ Percentage ≈ 15.82% = 16% in approx.

**∴ The number of students studying in class X from school P forms approximately 16% of the total number of students studying in class X from all schools together.**

questions.question: A thief running at 7 km/h is chased by a policeman whose speed is 12 km/h. If the thief is 280 m ahead of the policeman, then the time required for the policeman to catch the thief will be:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed of the thief = 7 km/h

Speed of the policeman = 12 km/h

Distance between the thief and the policeman = 280 m

**Concept:**

Relative speed is the difference in speeds when two objects move in the same direction.

**Formula used:**

Time = Distance / Relative Speed

**Calculation:**

Convert distance into km:

⇒ 280 m = 280/1000 km = 0.28 km

Calculate relative speed:

⇒ Relative Speed = 12 km/h - 7 km/h = 5 km/h

Calculate time required to catch the thief:

⇒ Time = Distance / Relative Speed

⇒ Time = 0.28 km / 5 km/h

⇒ Time = 0.056 hours

Convert time into minutes:

⇒ Time = 0.056 × 60 minutes

⇒ Time = 3.36 minutes

Convert decimal minutes into fraction:

⇒ Time = 3 (9/25) minutes

**∴ The time required for the policeman to catch the thief is 3 (9/25) minutes.**

questions.question: A can do a work in 20 days and B in 30 days. If they work on it together for 2 days, then what is the fraction of the work that is left?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can do a work in 20 days.

B can do a work in 30 days.

They work together for 2 days.

**Concept Used:**

When two or more individuals work together, their combined work rate is the sum of their individual work rates.

**Formula Used:**

Work rate of A = 1/20 work/day

Work rate of B = 1/30 work/day

Combined work rate = (1/20 + 1/30) work/day

Fraction of work done = Combined work rate × Number of days they work together

Fraction of work left = 1 - Fraction of work done

**Calculation:**

Combined work rate = 1/20 + 1/30

⇒ Combined work rate = 3/60 + 2/60

⇒ Combined work rate = 5/60 = 1/12 work/day

Fraction of work done in 2 days = (1/12) × 2

⇒ Fraction of work done = 1/6

Fraction of work left = 1 - 1/6

⇒ Fraction of work left = 6/6 - 1/6

⇒ Fraction of work left = 5/6

**∴ The fraction of the work that is left is 5/6.**

questions.question: A man wishes to cover 1 km distance in river water. In still water he takes 12 minutes to cover it, but in the flowing river he takes 13 minutes. The speed of the flowing water of the river is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance = 1 km

Time in still water = 12 minutes

Time in flowing water = 13 minutes

**Concept Used:**

Speed = Distance / Time

**Formula Used:**

Speed in still water = Distance / Time in still water

Speed in flowing water = Distance / Time in flowing water

Speed of river flow = Speed in flowing water - Speed in still water

**Calculation:**

Speed in still water = 1 km / 12 minutes = 1 km / (12/60 hours) = 1 km / 0.2 hours = 5 km/h

Speed in flowing water = 1 km / 13 minutes = 1 km / (13/60 hours) = 1 km / 0.2167 hours ≈ 4.615 km/h

⇒ Speed of river flow = Speed in still water - Speed in flowing water

⇒ Speed of river flow = 5 km/h - 4.615 km/h

⇒ Speed of river flow ≈ 0.385 km/h

⇒ Speed of river flow ≈ (5/13) km/h

**∴ The speed of the flowing water of the river is (5/13) km/h.**

questions.question: A train covers 60 km at a speed of 80 km/h, 100 km at a speed of 90 km/h, and another 140 km at a speed of 120 km/h. Find the average speed for the complete journey. (Round to the nearest integer.)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Distance 1 = 60 km, Speed 1 = 80 km/h

Distance 2 = 100 km, Speed 2 = 90 km/h

Distance 3 = 140 km, Speed 3 = 120 km/h

**Concept Used:**

To find the average speed, we need the total distance and the total time.

**Formula Used:**

Total distance = Distance 1 + Distance 2 + Distance 3

Total time = (Distance 1 / Speed 1) + (Distance 2 / Speed 2) + (Distance 3 / Speed 3)

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

**Calculation:**

Total distance = 60 km + 100 km + 140 km

⇒ Total distance = 300 km

Total time = (60 km / 80 km/h) + (100 km / 90 km/h) + (140 km / 120 km/h)

⇒ Total time = 0.75 h + 1.11 h + 1.17 h

⇒ Total time = 3.03 hours

Average speed = Total distance / Total time

⇒ Average speed = 300 km / 3.03 hours

⇒ Average speed = 99 km/h

**∴ The average speed for the complete journey is 99 km/h.**

questions.question: From an external point A, tangents AP and AQ are drawn to a circle with centre O. If ∠APQ = 40°, then find ∠POQ.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

From an external point A, tangents AP and AQ are drawn to a circle with centre O.

∠APQ = 40º

**Concept Used:**

The angle between the tangents drawn from an external point to a circle is equal to the angle subtended by the line segment joining the points of contact at the center.

**Calculation:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/00353dfe012561af414590108b6d7c31cc576eb823ecaac8f790731cb09f2ff6.png] 

Let ∠POQ be the angle subtended at the center by the tangents.

We know that the angle between the tangents (∠APQ) is equal to half the angle subtended by the line segment joining the points of contact at the center.

⇒ ∠POQ = 2 × ∠APQ

⇒ ∠POQ = 2 × 40º

⇒ ∠POQ = 80º

**∴ The angle ∠POQ is 80º.**

questions.question: 57% of Ranita’s weekly income is equal to 76% of Bhaskar’s weekly income. If Ranita’s weekly income was reduced by Rs. 400, while Bhaskar’s weekly income did not change, the ratio of the weekly incomes of Ranita and Bhaskar, respectively, would have been 6 : 5. What is Bhaskar’s weekly income (in Rs.)?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

57% of Ranita's weekly income = 76% of Bhaskar's weekly income

Ranita's weekly income reduced by Rs. 400

Ratio of weekly incomes of Ranita and Bhaskar = 6:5

**Concept Used:**

We need to set up equations based on the given percentages and ratio, then solve for Bhaskar's weekly income.

**Formula Used:**

Let Ranita's weekly income be R and Bhaskar's weekly income be B.

57% of R = 76% of B

(57/100)R = (76/100)B

R - 400 = (6/5)B

**Calculation:**

(57/100)R = (76/100)B

⇒ 57R = 76B ...(1)

R - 400 = (6/5)B

⇒ 5R - 2000 = 6B ...(2)

From equation (1):

⇒ R = (76/57)B

Substitute R in equation (2):

⇒ 5(76/57)B - 2000 = 6B

⇒ (380/57)B - 2000 = 6B

⇒ (380/57)B - 6B = 2000

⇒ (380B - 342B) / 57 = 2000

⇒ 38B / 57 = 2000

⇒ 38B = 2000 × 57

⇒ 38B = 114000

⇒ B = 114000 / 38

⇒ B = 3000

**∴ Bhaskar's weekly income is Rs. 3000.**

questions.question: A person borrowed Rs. 1760 at 6% per annum and Rs. 2240 at 9% per annum at simple interest for the same period. He had to pay Rs. 1536 in all as interest. Find the time (in years).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal 1 (P₁) = Rs. 1760

Rate 1 (R₁) = 6% per annum

Principal 2 (P₂) = Rs. 2240

Rate 2 (R₂) = 9% per annum

Total Interest = Rs. 1536

**Concept Used:**

Simple Interest (SI) = Principal (P) × Rate (R) × Time (T) / 100

**Formula Used:**

SI₁ = P₁ × R₁ × T / 100

SI₂ = P₂ × R₂ × T / 100

Total Interest = SI₁ + SI₂

**Calculation:**

SI₁ = 1760 × 6 × T / 100

⇒ SI₁ = 105.6T

SI₂ = 2240 × 9 × T / 100

⇒ SI₂ = 201.6T

Total Interest = SI₁ + SI₂

⇒ 1536 = 105.6T + 201.6T

⇒ 1536 = 307.2T

⇒ T = 1536 / 307.2

⇒ T = 5

**∴ The time period is 5 years.**

Ramanna purchased raw materials for a certain price to manufacture a product. However, owing to a shortage of labour, 22.5% of the raw materials could not be utilised and got wasted. 80% of the cost of raw materials used was added as the cost of manufacturing. If Ramanna could sell his product at a price to earn an overall profit of 20% after offering a discount of 20%, how many times of the total cost of the raw materials purchased was the marked price of the product?

[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the total raw material purchased cost = 100.

Material used = 100 − 22.5 = 77.5.

Total CP = Total raw material cost + Manufacturing cost = 100 + (80% of 77.5) = 100 + 62 = 162.

Using direct formula: CP ÷ MP = (100 − Discount%) ÷ (100 + Profit%) = (100 − 20) ÷ (100 + 20) = 80 ÷ 120 = 2 ÷ 3.

MP = 162 × (3 ÷ 2) = 243.

Ratio = MP ÷ Raw material cost = 243 ÷ 100 = 2.43.

**∴ The correct answer is 2.43 times.**

SP = MP × (1 − Discount%)

questions.question: If cot θ =28/45, then find the value of (sin θ - cos θ).
questions.solution:
**Given:**

If cot θ = 28/45, then find the value of (sin θ - cos θ).

**Concept:**

We need to find sin θ and cos θ using the given cot θ value and then calculate (sin θ - cos θ).

**Formula Used:**

cot θ = 1/tan θ

sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse

cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse

**Calculation:**

Given, cot θ = 28/45

⇒ tan θ = 1/(cot θ) = 45/28

⇒ Let opposite = 45, adjacent = 28

⇒ hypotenuse = √(opposite² + adjacent²)

⇒ hypotenuse = √(45² + 28²)

⇒ hypotenuse = √(2025 + 784)

⇒ hypotenuse = √2809

⇒ hypotenuse = 53

⇒ sin θ = opposite/hypotenuse = 45/53

⇒ cos θ = adjacent/hypotenuse = 28/53

⇒ sin θ - cos θ = (45/53) - (28/53)

⇒ sin θ - cos θ = (45 - 28)/53

⇒ sin θ - cos θ = 17/53

**∴ The correct answer is option 2.**

questions.question: A can complete a piece of work alone in 200 days, while B can complete the same piece of work alone in 100 days. In every three-day cycle, both A and B work on day 1, only A works on day 2, and only B works on day 3. This cycle continues till the work is completed. How many days in all does it take the duo to complete the work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

A can complete a piece of work alone in 200 days.

B can complete the same piece of work alone in 100 days.

In every three-day cycle:

- Both A and B work on day 1

- Only A works on day 2

- Only B works on day 3

**Concept:**

Calculate the work done in each 3-day cycle and then find the total number of cycles required to complete the work.

**Formula Used:**

Work done by A in 1 day = 1/200

Work done by B in 1 day = 1/100

**Calculation:**

Work done by A and B together on day 1:

⇒ (1/200) + (1/100) = 1/200 + 2/200 = 3/200

Work done by A on day 2:

⇒ 1/200

Work done by B on day 3:

⇒ 1/100

Total work done in each 3-day cycle:

⇒ 3/200 + 1/200 + 1/100 = 3/200 + 1/200 + 2/200 = 6/200 = 3/100

Total work to be done = 1 (whole work)

Number of 3-day cycles needed to complete the work:

⇒ Total work / Work done in each cycle = 1 / (3/100) = 100/3

Total days needed = Number of cycles × 3 days per cycle

⇒ (100/3) × 3 = 100 days

Since the work is completed in fractions of a cycle, we need to calculate the exact number of days:

100/3 = 33 cycles and 1/3 cycle remaining

For the remaining 1/3 cycle:

Day 1: Work done = 3/200 (A and B together)

Day 2: Work done = 1/200 (A alone)

Day 3: Work done = 1/100 (B alone)

Total work done in 1/3 cycle:

⇒ 1/3 × (3/200 + 1/200 + 1/100) = 1/3 × (3/100) = 1/100

Hence, the remaining work after 33 cycles:

⇒ 1 - (99/100) = 1/100

Additional day required to complete the remaining 1/100 of work by A alone:

⇒ 1/200 × 2 = 1/100

Total days:

⇒ 33 cycles × 3 days + 1 additional day = 99 + 2/3 days ≈ 99 (2/3) days

**∴ The correct answer is option 2: 99 (2/3) days.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

A alone completes work in = 200 days

B alone completes work in = 100 days

**Calculations:**

LCM of 200 and 100 = 200 (Total work = 200 units)

A’s 1 day work = 200 ÷ 200 = 1 unit

B’s 1 day work = 200 ÷ 100 = 2 units

Now, work in 3-day cycle:

Day 1: A + B = 1 + 2 = 3 units

Day 2: A = 1 unit

Day 3: B = 2 units

Total in 3 days = 3 + 1 + 2 = 6 units

We need 200 units, so:

⇒ 33 cycles (99 days) = 198 units

Remaining = 200 - 198 = 2 units

Next cycle: Day 1 (A + B) = 3 units > 2 units needed

So, Total days = 99 + 2/3 = 99 (2)/(3) days

**∴ The duo completes the work in 99 (2)/(3) days.**

questions.question: A 12 litre solution of acid and water contains 30% acid. How much water (in litres) must be added to get a solution having 20% acid?

Since only water is added, the quantity of acid remains constant.

Initial Volume × Initial Acid % = Final Volume × Final Acid %

Final Volume = (12 × 30) ÷ 20 = 18 litres

Water added = Final Volume − Initial Volume = 18 − 12 = 6 litres

⇒ In the new solution, acid quantity is still 3.6 litres but represents 20% of the total.

⇒ 20% of (12 + x) = 3.6

⇒ (20 ÷ 100) × (12 + x) = 3.6

⇒ (1 ÷ 5) × (12 + x) = 3.6

⇒ 12 + x = 3.6 × 5

⇒ 12 + x = 18

⇒ x = 18 − 12 = 6 litres

**∴ The correct answer is 6.**

questions.question: How many metres of cloth will be required to make a conical tent, the radius of whose base is 21 metres and height is 28 metres. The width of the cloth is 5 metres. (Where pi=(22)/(7))
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Radius of the base (r) = 21 metres

Height (h) = 28 metres

Width of the cloth = 5 metres

π = 22/7

**Concept:**

To find the amount of cloth required, we need to calculate the lateral surface area of the conical tent. The formula for the lateral surface area of a cone is:

Lateral Surface Area = πrl

where r is the radius and l is the slant height of the cone.

**Formula Used:**

First, find the slant height (l) using the Pythagorean theorem:

l = √(r² + h²)

**Calculation:**

We have:

⇒ r = 21 metres

⇒ h = 28 metres

Calculate the slant height (l):

⇒ l = √(21² + 28²)

⇒ l = √(441 + 784)

⇒ l = √1225

⇒ l = 35 metres

Now, calculate the lateral surface area:

⇒ Lateral Surface Area = πrl

⇒ Lateral Surface Area = (22/7) × 21 × 35

⇒ Lateral Surface Area = 22 × 3 × 35

⇒ Lateral Surface Area = 2310 square metres

Since the width of the cloth is 5 metres, find the length of the cloth needed:

⇒ Length of the cloth = Lateral Surface Area / Width

⇒ Length of the cloth = 2310 / 5

⇒ Length of the cloth = 462 metres

**∴ The correct answer is option 2, 462 metres.**

questions.question: In an election, 12% of the voters in the voter list did not cast their votes, whereas 84 voters cast their ballot papers blank. There were only two candidates: Ramagya and Shravan. The winner, Ramagya, was supported by 54% of all the voters in the list. He got 1456 more votes than his rival, Shravan. Find the total number of voters in the list.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

12% of voters did not cast their votes, 84 voters cast blank ballots. Ramagya supported by 54% of all voters, received 1456 more votes than Shravan.

**Concept Used:**

Percentage calculation and basic algebra.

**Formula Used:**

1. Total Votes = Total Voters × (Percentage of votes cast / 100)

2. Ramagya's Votes = Total Voters × (Percentage of support for Ramagya / 100)

3. Shravan's Votes = Ramagya's Votes - 1456

**Calculation:**

Let the total number of voters be V.

⇒ 88% of Voters cast their votes (since 12% did not vote)

⇒ Total Votes Cast = 0.88V

⇒ Ramagya's Votes = 0.54V

⇒ Shravan's Votes = 0.54V - 1456

Total Votes Cast = Ramagya's Votes + Shravan's Votes + Blank Votes

⇒ 0.88V = 0.54V + (0.54V - 1456) + 84

Simplifying the equation:

⇒ 0.88V = 1.08V - 1456 + 84

⇒ 0.88V = 1.08V - 1372

⇒ 1372 = 1.08V - 0.88V

⇒ 1372 = 0.20V

⇒ V = 1372 / 0.20

⇒ V = 6860

**∴ The total number of voters in the list is 6860.**

questions.question: If x + y + z = 1, xy + yz + zx = -1 and xyz = -1, then (x³ + y³ + z³) is equal to ________.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

x + y + z = 1

xy + yz + zx = -1

xyz = -1

**Formula used:**

x³ + y³ + z³ = (x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² - xy - yz - zx) + 3xyz

**Calculation:**

x² + y² + z² = (x + y + z)² - 2(xy + yz + zx)

⇒ x² + y² + z² = (1)² - 2(-1)

⇒ x² + y² + z² = 1 + 2

⇒ x² + y² + z² = 3

x³ + y³ + z³ = (x + y + z)(x² + y² + z² - xy - yz - zx) + 3xyz

⇒ x³ + y³ + z³ = (1)(3 - (-1)) + 3(-1)

⇒ x³ + y³ + z³ = (1)(4) - 3

⇒ x³ + y³ + z³ = 4 - 3

⇒ x³ + y³ + z³ = 1

**∴ x³ + y³ + z³ = 1**

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, one got 60% of the total valid votes. 25% of the votes were invalid. If the total number of votes was 15,000, then find the number of valid votes that the other candidate got.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Total number of votes = 15,000

Invalid votes = 25%

Votes received by one candidate = 60% of valid votes

**Formula Used:**

Valid votes = Total votes × (1 - Invalid vote percentage)

Votes received by the other candidate = Valid votes - Votes received by one candidate

**Calculation:**

Invalid votes percentage = 25% = 0.25

Valid votes percentage = 1 - 0.25 = 0.75

Valid votes = 15000 × 0.75

⇒ Valid votes = 11250

Votes received by one candidate = 60% of 11250

⇒ Votes received by one candidate = 0.60 × 11250

⇒ Votes received by one candidate = 6750

Votes received by the other candidate = 11250 - 6750

⇒ Votes received by the other candidate = 4500

**The number of valid votes that the other candidate got is 4500.**

⇒ (x)/(y) = 2

**The ratio AB : AC is 2 : 1.**
